newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE AIMS TO PLAY MORE IN THE U.S. NEXT YEAR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE AIMS TO PLAY MORE IN THE U.S. NEXT YEAR.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie, certain to finish European number one for the fourth successive year, plans to play more in the United States next year in his bid to land his first major.
After shooting a seven-under-par 65 in the third round of the German Masters on Saturday, Montgomerie admitted winning a major was his "big goal".
"I shall play a bit more in the United States next year...because my biggest target is to win my first major. That would take a weight off my mind.
"The next major is not for another six months but I would be thrilled if I am playing like I am now when I get to the U.S. Masters at Augusta."
Montgomerie finished two shots adrift of joint leaders Peter Baker and Paul Broadhurst on 202.
He has only to finish in the top 40 in Berlin to clinch top spot on the European money list.
Though he intends to spend more time in the U.S. next year, Scotsman Montgomerie said he would be playing the same number of European events as he has done this season.
"So I hope to be going for the European record of being number one five times in a row...that would be fabulous," he said.
Englishman Baker's best-of-the day 64 included nine birdies.
